(1) Blocking: a 401 or 501 whose body is cut short was retried. Now, once the status has arrived, that status decides. StatusBeforeBody.answer() catches any error raised after the response hook ran on a non-2xx and returns that status with an empty body, as pi does with response.text().catch(() => ''). It also forgets the previous request's status first, and reads it through _arrived() so pyright does not narrow it. A 2xx whose body fails raises as before: cut short, it is retried as a dropped connection (pi's 'terminated'); a broken encoding fails at once. The same rule now covers the Copilot device-flow poll: a cut-short 401 ends the login there instead of being polled through.

(2) CHANGELOG now says 'one of those statuses' and adds the cut-short and read-timeout cases. The refused text for an unreadable 401 or 403 is byte-identical to the text the same status gets with an empty body, at all three sites. It differs from 8f7d98aa's text, which quoted the decoder's or the connection's error, and the CHANGELOG and ADR 12.2 item 5 say so.

(3) Added rows for WriteTimeout (the classifier, each site, and a retried-to-success row per provider) and for the Copilot poll's hook (verify r3 G7).

Docs: ADR-0251 has an updated status line, 12.2 headline, item 1 and item 5, and a new section 12.7. The decisions README row and the CHANGELOG are updated. The guides were left as they are: their wording is still true.

blocking.title: Six texts say only a failure before any status arrived counts as 'could not be reached', but a 2xx whose body breaks is retried that way
blocking.detail: The code retries a 200 whose body is cut short or times out. The status arrived, and the error then reaches the transport branch ('could not be reached (RemoteProtocolError/ReadTimeout)'). This matches pi, because Node fetch reports 'terminated' and a timeout. ADR 12.7 item 1 and the StatusBeforeBody docstring state this exception. These texts state the rule without it, so they are false for this case: CHANGELOG.md:308 ('only a failure before any status arrived counts as not reached'), ADR-0251:935 (12.2 headline), ADR-0251:953 (12.2 item 1, 'the transport set above decides only a failure before any status'), the README 0251 row ('상태 전 실패만 "연결 불가"'), the _helpers.py:317 _TRANSIENT_TRANSPORT comment, and the commit message ('only a failure before any status arrived reaches that branch'). The auth_storage docstring's 'a 2xx that is not a token -> None' is also too broad. The round's DECISION text says the same literal rule. So either keep the pi-like retry and add the 2xx exception to those six texts (text-only fix), or follow the literal rule in code. This needs a deliberate choice; the goal requires every text to be true.
blocking.evidence: Live on d7f25e1a, real aelix --mode json -p, fake expired login, raw-socket token recorder: plans tr200,200 and sl200,200 (2 s timeout) for openai-codex, anthropic and github-copilot each gave rc 0, auto_retry_start [(1,2000)], auto_retry_end [(True,1)], the refreshed token sent. The error texts read 'peer closed connection without sending complete message body' and 'ReadTimeout'. See .omc/probes/379-live/r4verify/logs/matrix_tree.out. Node 26 fetch, which is pi's transport: tr200 makes json() throw 'TypeError: terminated', and sl200 throws TimeoutError (logs/node_fetch_probe.out).
